text: For once the entire town touched grass at the same time

All debts got forgiven, which sounds super generous until you clock that the collectors had logged off too
The main beef: the finale dropped before anybody finished their side quests
Anything liftable got handed to whoever had the arms for it, and the heavy stuff stayed put with a little note saying whose it was, provenance core
Every door left wide open, the open-door policy finally hard launched
The snacks got passed around until the snacks were no more, communal munch era down to the last crumb
Most people wanted to spend it with the fam, and the universe actually let them have that one
Everybody dropped whatever was in their hands, the grind officially paused mid-swing
The kids got the speedrun version of the lore
A whole home-cooked dinner went cold on the table while the fam who made it stood outside staring up, dinner left on read

Saved to the vault: one of everything plus a copy of the names, the ultimate backup

The works won't open Monday, the forever weekend is real and it's here

Down the pub they're saying they always knew it would end like this, which is the exact take they had last week too

On the final broadcast a dance band played to an empty studio and still ate

Not the tax office sending its final demands bang on schedule at the literal end of the world
Region by region the network logged off, and every group chat went grey in turn
Phones went full do-not-disturb, and not one ring was left in the whole town
The last trend ever was sky pics, most of the final posts just the sky, and honestly it ate
Every balance froze at midnight, final scores locked, the leaderboard is closed

The feeds are saying the corporations knew the whole time and sold tickets, conspiracy brain to the very end

The fusion plants idled down one by one and the city did a three-night slow fade into the dark
In the arcades, the kids who'd run the same game every night for years ran it back one last time together, then left the cabinets on, demo screens looping for an empty room
Block by block the whole skyline logged off, screens going dark like the city hit sleep mode
Every server farm kept grinding as long as the power held, humming to itself in the dark with nobody left to grind for
People stayed logged in till the very end, doing one last deep scroll through years of their own posts and pics
Every personal file goes to the permanent archive, nothing gets deleted, your camera roll lives forever
The final mass text went to every address the city ever had, even the long-dead ones, and it said thank you and goodbye in every language anyone there ever spoke
The orbital yards clocked out for good and the ship line went still
Every launch got scrubbed, the countdowns left hanging on whatever number they hit
The last shuttle up packed seed stock, photos and basically nothing else, carry-on only
Stations mothballed, crews sent home, orbits logged: the shutdown checklist got speedrun
All craft: back to the dock and power down, joyriding era officially over
The moon base got left out of the group chat yet again and is salty it heard last
Up on the station they say the view has never been this goated
The belt mining crews clocked out and rolled home for good
The ring station got turned so its windows faced home, and the crew took turns in the window seats through the last watch
Up in orbit the satellites were left running solo, still beaming down weather pics over cities where the streets had emptied and the lights went out one district at a time
Mission control signed off for good, the cleanest mic drop in the program's history
The crew on the far side of the moon got the news last of all over a laggy signal and wrote down every single word by hand
All the fuel got poured back into the tanks, rocket juice returned to sender
The orbital hotel refunded every booking, minus a handling fee, because of course it did
Kids at the observation windows gave every incoming ship the full wholesome wave until the last one docked

Out past the last charted star something stirred, like a sleeper rolling over when a door shuts somewhere else in the house, the creepiest wake-up call ever logged

The dark pulled up a little closer, no invite needed

Whatever waits at the end of all roads got told the colony was on its way, and the last thing the long-range instruments caught before powering down was a patch of sky gone dead silent, not even background noise
The crew are big mad that {subject} never spilled what comes after

The stars just kept on starring, unbothered by any of it
Air fine, power dipping, every soul on the headcount, the last vibe check passed
{subject} was the last one left at the party, still up in the dark after the colony's last lights went out and the crew had gone to their berths
The instruments kept on recording long after anyone stopped reading, performing for an audience of zero
The colony clocked off its watch for the last time
{subject} kept a perfectly neutral aura to the end, serving no comfort and no blame
Way past the colony's instruments, where only one probe still checked in, the thing it had been warned about for four ages turned away in zero hurry, and the probe lost it within the hour
Engineering stayed in character to the end and filed one last maintenance ticket, marked urgent
The colonists took turns sitting with {subject} through the last watch, and whatever got said is locked lore none of them could repeat afterwards
The kids snoozed straight through the apocalypse, sleep schedule undefeated
The hydroponics bays were left lit so the plants could keep their glow
At the end {subject} had the comms all to itself, the only voice left, doing a solo set

Your name became the final track on the beacon's loop
Long after the last lights went out the beacon kept posting on loop to a feed with zero followers left
After eighty years of warnings the beacon just low-key added the colony to its list, no fanfare

For a few seconds the dead colony's beacon and the living colony's last transmission went full duet, two recordings of the end playing over each other on one frequency, and then the living one went quiet
The comms officer is deadass sure the beacon said goodbye
Beacon still posting, colony on permanent mute
The relay absorbed the colony into its geometry, no take-backs, and went silent
The linguists stayed locked in at their posts, translating the last of it
The relay's hum locked onto a single note and refused to switch tracks
Plot twist from the linguists: the relay had said this before, and the colony's own name was already in its oldest geometry, filed among peoples who ended long before anyone here learned to talk

Keep the relay powered after we've all logged off for good
Your future self left you on read this time
One last message dropped from nine years out, and it was just the sound of your own breathing, no caption
Your future self said this is the part you always forget, so please, no pressure, try to remember it this time

Your future self swore it was all worth it, and you chose to be delulu enough to believe it
In the last hour a message came from nine years out in your own handwriting, the letters a little off from a hand out of practice, and all it said was that it was glad you waited up
Your unmade self slid in and took your hand
This is how mine ended too, it said, and its grip stayed locked in
The branch you stood on and the branch that ended finally linked up
Your unmade self came all this way to see if this branch ends the way its own did, stuck around to watch it happen, and seemed almost relieved to have a plus one
The other you never explains itself, and half the station has the ick about it
Every door on the station got unlocked, by order, so the other you could free roam wherever it liked
